title: Anticoagulant rat poison (superwarfarin, e.g. Ratex) poisoning
population: Adults and children (one pathway; ADULT / CHILD lines where thresholds and doses differ)

admission.title: Diagnostic criteria — any one confirms exposure

items.t: Ingestion of anticoagulant rat poison (pellets, granules, wedges, blocks, powder) — packet seen
Unexplained bleeding or bruising + raised INR (bleeding may be occult)
Onset of coagulopathy is delayed: ADULT 1–2 days, CHILD 48–72 h. A normal INR on arrival does not exclude it.
Rat poison ≠ warfarin: superwarfarins are more potent, act for weeks to months, may resist large vitamin K1 doses; prolonged vitamin K1 via Poisons Centre / haematologist
Warfarin-therapy reversal rules do not apply to rat poison
Not all rat poison is anticoagulant: unspecified rat poison or pesticide → also consider amitraz and organophosphates
"Two-step" street poison = aldicarb (carbamate) → cholinergic → OP pathway

Patient on therapeutic warfarin / prosthetic valve → specialist

admission.title: Red flags to rule out on arrival

decision.t: 10. Bleeding → plasma + IV vitamin K1; REFER if uncontrolled / intracranial

11. ADMIT (asymptomatic child, small amount, able to return: may observe as outpatient) — stabilise, then continue on the 0 h – discharge inpatient chart and the 24-hour nursing record. Notify NMC: rodenticide superwarfarin poisoning is notifiable.

chart.phase_note: INR timing counts from the time of ingestion, not arrival. Rows from Day 4 apply while vitamin K1 is still needed.

standing.t: HR, BP, GCS + bleeding check (gums, nose, skin / new bruises, puncture sites) 4-hourly; hourly while actively bleeding or receiving plasma
Each urine and stool: blood / melaena; urine dipstick daily
Record every vitamin K1 dose and every INR time and result
No IM injections, no NSAIDs or aspirin
Firm pressure on puncture sites · ask about headache

rows.label: 0 h
rows.lead: Check the referral note for vitamin K1, plasma or charcoal already given — do not duplicate. Identify the product from the packet. Call Poisons Helpline 0861 555 777 or UFS 082 491 0160 (24 h).

feed.t: Do NOT give vitamin K1 prophylactically — only for active bleeding or a raised INR
ADULT: lyophilised plasma or FFP 15 mL/kg IV + vitamin K1 10 mg slow IV (undiluted, not mixed)
CHILD: lyophilised plasma or FFP 20 mL/kg IV + vitamin K1 1–5 mg/dose IV slowly
ADULT, not on anticoagulants, INR > 4: vitamin K1 10–20 mg oral
CHILD, INR > 2.5: vitamin K1 1–5 mg/dose oral (IV only if rapid reversal needed)
The IV ampoule may be given orally

tests.t: INR / PT baseline — ADULT all; CHILD if symptoms / signs
Record time of ingestion on the request form
Ward Hb / VBG · FBC incl. platelets
Group and crossmatch if bleeding
U&E, LFT
Urine dipstick for blood
If intentional: paracetamol level (≥ 4 h)
If female of child-bearing age: urine βhCG
If cholinergic signs: pseudocholinesterase → OP pathway

treatment.t: Resuscitate: airway, breathing, circulation
Plasma + IV vitamin K1 (vitamin K1 column)
Packed cells per transfusion guideline
Headache, vomiting, falling GCS, focal signs = intracranial bleed: plasma + IV vitamin K1, then REFER for CT
Bleeding not controlled: REFER
Stop warfarin if on therapy

treatment.h: Activated charcoal — best within 1 h, airway protected

treatment.t: ADULT 50 g in 100 mL water
CHILD < 6 y: 1 g/kg in 50–100 mL; > 6 y: 20–50 g in 100–300 mL
Unspecified rat poison: look for OP / amitraz toxidrome
Notify NMC (rodenticide superwarfarin is notifiable)
Asymptomatic child, small amount, able to return: may observe as outpatient; INR at 36–72 h
Start the 24-hour nursing record

Then INR 4–6-hourly until stable

feed.t: If on vitamin K1: repeat per INR

tests.t: INR 4–6-hourly until stable, then 24-hourly
Hb daily while bleeding or on vitamin K1

Hb if bled

items.t: No prophylactic vitamin K1 — bleeding or raised INR only
ADULT bleeding: plasma (lyophilised or FFP) 15 mL/kg IV + vitamin K1 10 mg slow IV
ADULT INR > 4, no bleeding: vitamin K1 10–20 mg oral
CHILD bleeding: plasma 20 mL/kg IV + vitamin K1 1–5 mg/dose IV slowly
CHILD INR > 2.5: vitamin K1 1–5 mg/dose, oral preferred
IV vitamin K1 may cause hypersensitivity — give slowly; IV ampoule can be given orally
Bleeding: stop warfarin; plasma + vitamin K1 5 mg slow IV
INR 5–8: stop warfarin · INR > 8: vitamin K1 0.5–1 mg oral, repeat at 12–24 h if still ≥ 8
Consult a haematologist; prosthetic valve: specialist
More potent; small doses of concentrated forms can anticoagulate significantly
Long duration: vitamin K1 may be needed for weeks to several months; may resist large doses
Onset delayed (ADULT 1–2 d, CHILD 48–72 h): a normal arrival INR does not exclude poisoning
The low-dose warfarin-therapy rules (INR 5–8 / > 8) do not apply to a rat-poison patient
INR normal on vitamin K1 ≠ cured — recheck after each dose reduction and after stopping
Examples on packets: brodifacoum, bromadiolone, difenacoum

items.h: Not all rat poison is anticoagulant

items.t: Unspecified rat poison or pesticide: also consider amitraz and organophosphates
"Two-step" street poison = aldicarb (carbamate) → cholinergic → OP pathway
Unknown product: call the Poisons Helpline; check INR anyway
HR rising / BP falling from the patient's baseline
Reaction during IV vitamin K1 or plasma: stop, treat
Suspected intracranial bleed: plasma + IV vitamin K1 first, then CT
Bleeding not controlled with plasma + vitamin K1
Antidote unavailable; psychiatric evaluation after self-harm
INR · Hb / FBC · group and crossmatch · U&E
Salivation, sweating, pinpoint pupils, fasciculations → OP pathway

discharge.title: Discharge criteria — all must be met (conditional items where they apply)

items.t: INR reviewed at 48 h (ADULT) / 36–72 h (CHILD) after ingestion
If on vitamin K1: INR stable on oral dose; dose and duration agreed with PIC / haematologist
Vitamin K1 supply + INR dates given
Intentional: mental health assessment and plan
CHILD: home circumstances assessed, safe storage counselled
Returns if bleeding; can reach the hospital
On vitamin K1: INR on the agreed dates; continue until INR stays normal off vitamin K1 (weeks–months)
Return at once: bleeding gums / nose, blood in urine, black stool, severe headache, drowsiness

items.t: Hourly while actively bleeding or receiving plasma
Ask about headache; note vomiting or confusion
Gums, nose, skin / new bruises, puncture sites
Each urine and stool: blood / melaena; urine dipstick daily
Firm pressure on puncture sites; no IM injections

Give IV vitamin K1 slowly — watch for a reaction
Write the time each INR is drawn; no NSAIDs or aspirin

Headache, vomiting, confusion, falling GCS or seizure
A reaction during IV vitamin K1 or plasma
